incompressible Navier–Stokes equations that starts from rest and develops unbounded velocity
in finite time while maintaining uniformly bounded kinetic energy.

For every nu > 0 there exist a force f in C^infty_c(R^3 x (0, infinity); R^3), a compact set K subset R^3, and smooth velocity and pressure fields u, p on R^3 x [0,1) satisfying  d_t u + (u . grad) u - nu Laplacian u + grad p = f,  div u = 0,  u(.,0) = 0,   (1.1)  such that supp u(.,t) union supp p(.,t) subset K for every 0 <= t < 1,  sup_{0<=t<1} ||u(t)||_{L^2(R^3)} < infinity,  limsup_{t -> 1^-} ||u(t)||_{L^infinity(R^3)} = infinity. theorem_1_1_assertions_enumerated: A1. f in C^infty_c(R^3 x (0,infinity); R^3) exists — smooth, compactly supported in space AND in time, vanishing near t = 0.

A2. A compact set K subset R^3 exists with supp u(.,t) union supp p(.,t) subset K for EVERY 0 <= t < 1 — the SOLUTION and the PRESSURE are compactly supported in space, uniformly in t, not merely decaying.
A3. u, p are smooth on R^3 x [0,1) and solve (1.1) exactly with u(.,0) = 0.
A4. sup_{0<=t<1} ||u(t)||_{L^2} < infinity — uniformly bounded kinetic energy on the whole interval of existence.
A6. Consequently: NO smooth solution (u,P) on R^3 x [0,infinity) with the same force and initial datum has uniformly bounded kinetic energy.

gate.question: Is the theorem as reported in arc 5 the theorem the manuscript states?
gate.answer_status: UNVERIFIED (§3f rule 1 — this session read the manuscript and also wrote this gate answer; no fresh session has re-derived it).

differences.arc5: 'a smooth, compactly supported force f and a time T'; no viscosity quantifier anywhere in the reported statement or in the banked JSON fields.
differences.manuscript: 'For every nu > 0 there exist a force f ... and smooth velocity and pressure fields u,p on R^3 x [0,1)'. The viscosity is quantified UNIVERSALLY and the singular time is FIXED at T = 1.
differences.why_it_matters: Fefferman's (C) opens 'Take nu > 0 and n = 3', i.e. it is enough to answer one viscosity. The manuscript proves MORE than (C) asks, by an explicit rescaling (10.22). Arc 5 reported neither the surplus nor the fixed T.

differences.severity: MATERIAL — AND IT IS THE ONE THAT TOUCHES THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN WALL
differences.arc5: silent. No banked field records any support property of the SOLUTION.
differences.manuscript: 'a compact set K subset R^3 ... such that supp u(.,t) union supp p(.,t) subset K for every 0 <= t < 1'.
differences.why_it_matters: The velocity and pressure are COMPACTLY SUPPORTED IN SPACE, uniformly in time, not merely finite-energy or fast-decaying. Fefferman's (4) and (7) are then discharged by containment rather than by any decay estimate, and the SAME property is what Corollary 10.6 uses to periodize. W4 is this repository's localisation problem; the manuscript's object never has one, because it is compactly supported by construction from the start of §10.

differences.arc5: '(A) and (B) are untouched. The unforced problem is open. So is (D).'
differences.manuscript: 'Compact support also yields the corresponding construction on T^3 = R^3/Z^3, establishing alternative (D) in [13]; see Corollary 10.6.' Corollary 10.6 is stated and proved at pp. 125-126. The Lean project's formalization.yaml declares navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic as a proved main result.
differences.why_it_matters: (D) IS NOT UNTOUCHED. It is claimed, in the same manuscript, as a corollary. W4's ONLY unbroken break clause is (c), and clause (c) IS statement (D) (WALLS.md W4; STATE.md). Arc 5's charter item A6-D calls (D) 'the nearest unclaimed Fefferman statement'. On the manuscript's own text it is claimed. This does not by itself make it true; it makes arc 5's sentence false as a report of the manuscript.

limsup, not lim. The manuscript asserts unboundedness along a sequence, and the proof exhibits it along an explicit path x_tau = (sqrt(2) X_in tau, 0, 0), t = 1 - tau, eq. (10.20)-(10.21). 'Becomes unbounded' is a fair gloss; it is not the statement.

differences.arc5: the energy clause is reported as a property of the constructed solution only.
differences.manuscript: there are TWO energy clauses: the constructed u satisfies sup_{0<=t<1}||u(t)||_{L^2} < infinity, AND the theorem's operative conclusion is a NON-EXISTENCE statement — 'there is no smooth solution (u,P) on R^3 x [0,infinity) with the same force and initial datum whose kinetic energy is uniformly bounded'.
differences.why_it_matters: Fefferman's (C) is a non-existence statement, not an exhibition. The manuscript states it in that form; arc 5 reported only the exhibition half. An exhibition does not answer (C) without the comparison argument (Lemma 10.5) that transfers the growth to any competitor.

differences.arc5: 'A separate 112-page preprint (Alpoge-Buckmaster) constructs finite-time blowup for FORCED 3D Euler ... developed with substantial LLM iteration using Anthropic models'.
differences.manuscript: OpenAI's companion is a 57-page manuscript, 'FINITE TIME BLOWUP FOR THE EULER EQUATION', OPENAI, whose Theorem 1.1 is UNFORCED: 'There exists u_0 in C^infty_{c,sigma}(R^3) such that 0 < T_*(u_0) < infinity.'
differences.why_it_matters: Arc 5's Euler row describes a DIFFERENT manuscript by different authors. This repository has now fetched OpenAI's own Euler manuscript and it claims strictly more than arc 5's row: unforced, smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data on R^3. Arc 5's row is not thereby refuted — the Alpoge-Buckmaster preprint may also exist — but arc 5 banked no OpenAI Euler result and one exists.

differences.manuscript: MEASURED. The Navier-Stokes manuscript's bibliography has 22 numbered entries and Chen-Hou is NOT among them. The Euler manuscript DOES cite Chen and Hou (entries [6],[7] of its bibliography, 'proved blowup in an axially periodic cylinder with an impermeable wall, combining analysis with rigorous numerical estimates'). Cordoba-Martinez-Zoroa IS cited in the Navier-Stokes manuscript, three times: [6] arXiv:2309.08495, [7] arXiv:2410.22920, [8] ARMA 250 (2026) 38.
differences.why_it_matters: Arc 5 recorded the criticism at press level. At primary the criticism is accurate for the Navier-Stokes manuscript and inaccurate for the pair of manuscripts taken together. Whether Chen-Hou is USED in the Navier-Stokes argument, and therefore owed a citation there, is A6-AUDIT gate item 4 and is NOT answered by this unit.

fefferman_conditions_claimed_clause_by_c.consequence_for_this_repository: The manuscript's discharge of (4),(5),(8),(9) and (7) is by CONTAINMENT: compact spatial support of u, p and f, and compact temporal support of f. Not one of those five conditions is discharged by a decay estimate. W4 — 'A DSS profile on R^3 has infinite global energy; Clay condition (7) demands bounded energy' — is a statement about a DSS profile. The manuscript's object is not DSS on R^3 in that sense: it is a SELF-SIMILAR CORE inside a compactly supported field, and the compact support is imposed by cutoffs in Section 10 with the residual paid to f. Whether that mechanism transfers to a DSS profile this repository actually holds is U5's question and is NOT answered here.
